name: Google Cloud
scope_notes: Covers Google Cloud (IAM, API Keys, Cloud Storage). Covers Google Cloud project/org credentials; org policy constraints and VPC Service Controls need an organization resource; Workspace user OAuth and domain-wide delegation are in the separate `google` platform.

controls.name: iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation (legacy iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation)
controls.what: Blocks creation of new service account keys and SA HMAC keys.
controls.setting: Organization policies > constraint; gcloud resource-manager org-policies enable-enforce

controls.name: iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload
controls.what: Blocks uploading external public keys to service accounts.

controls.name: constraints/iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours
controls.what: Sets an expiry (1h to 2160h) for newly created SA keys.

controls.name: iam.serviceAccountKeyExposureResponse
controls.what: Auto-disables SA keys and SA-bound API keys that Google detects as exposed.

controls.name: constraints/iam.allowServiceAccountCredentialLifetimeExtension
controls.what: Lists SAs allowed to mint tokens longer than 1 hour (up to 12 hours).

controls.name: Service Account Token Creator role
controls.what: Only principals granted this role on an SA can mint its short-lived tokens.
controls.setting: IAM policy on the service account

controls.name: Disable service account (serviceAccounts.disable)
controls.what: Immediately disables the SA, which is the documented way to cut off already-issued short-lived tokens.

controls.name: Delete / disable service account key
controls.what: Stops the key from minting new tokens; tokens already minted stay valid until expiry.

controls.name: constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders
controls.what: Allow-lists which external IdP issuers can be configured.

controls.name: constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolAwsAccounts
controls.what: Allow-lists which AWS accounts can federate.

controls.name: Attribute conditions
controls.what: CEL condition on the provider limits which external tokens (e.g. which GitHub org) can be exchanged.

controls.name: Disable / delete workload identity pool
controls.what: Disabling or deleting the pool stops its identities from accessing Google Cloud.
controls.setting: IAM > Workload Identity Pools > Status toggle / Delete

controls.name: iam.managed.disableServiceAccountApiKeyCreation
controls.what: Blocks binding API keys to service accounts except for allowed services.
controls.setting: Organization policies > Block service account API key bindings

controls.name: API key application and API restrictions
controls.what: Restricts a key to listed external IPs, referrers or apps, and to specific APIs.
controls.setting: APIs & Services > Credentials > key > Application restrictions / API restrictions

controls.name: Delete API key
controls.what: Deletes the key; it can be restored for 30 days.

controls.name: constraints/storage.restrictAuthTypes
controls.what: Rejects user-account and/or service-account HMAC-signed requests to Cloud Storage.

controls.name: Deactivate / delete HMAC key
controls.what: Set the key INACTIVE or delete it; deleted keys are invalid immediately.
controls.setting: Cloud Storage > Settings > Interoperability; hmacKeys update/delete

controls.name: VPC Service Controls
controls.what: Service perimeters with ingress rules limit API access by network origin and identity, even with stolen credentials.

controls.name: constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders (Deny All)
controls.what: Org policy rule set to Deny All blocks creating new workload identity pool providers; exceptions can allow trusted providers per project. Same constraint as the existing limit_scope entry, used as a block.

no_control.what: Deleting a key does not revoke access tokens already minted from it.
Issued short-lived tokens cannot be revoked individually; only disabling/deleting the SA cuts them off.
Keys never expire unless the expiry org policy is set.

controls_unknown: Whether existing keys created before iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours was set get an expiry (docs say 'newly created').
Whether API keys support an expiry setting.
Which audit field identifies the API key or HMAC access ID used on a data-plane request.
Whether GetKeyString/lookupKey calls are logged for keys.lookupKey.
Plan/pricing for VPC Service Controls (needs organization).

authentication.summary: A JSON (or P12) private key for a service account. The holder signs a JWT and exchanges it for an OAuth 2.0 access token, then calls Google APIs as the service account.

federation.details: Keys authenticate the service account directly. Context-Aware Access policies 'apply only to users', so IdP/CAA conditions on human users do not gate key use. No doc states an SSO check on keys.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP list on the key itself. VPC Service Controls perimeters with ingress rules (by identity and IP) restrict API requests to protected services; services outside the perimeter are not covered.

lifetime.summary: Never expire by default; iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours can set 1h-2160h (90 days) for new keys

renewal.expiry_basis: Key reused to mint new 1-hour access tokens until the key is deleted, disabled or expires
renewal.summary: Rotate by creating a new key and deleting the old one (up to 10 keys per SA).

administration.summary: Org policy can block key creation and key upload; for orgs created on/after 2024-05-03 creation is blocked by default. Exposed keys are auto-disabled by default.
administration.conditions: Org policies need an organization resource.

offboard.details: Keys belong to a service account; access ends when the service account is disabled or deleted, not when a user leaves.

inventory.details: Cloud Asset Inventory supports iam.googleapis.com/ServiceAccountKey in its list/search/export APIs across an organization.

inventory.ui: Security > Asset Inventory > Resource search, filter asset type iam.googleapis.com/ServiceAccountKey; per SA: IAM & Admin > Service accounts > (SA) > Keys

usage.ui: Logging > Logs Explorer, filter protoPayload.authenticationInfo.serviceAccountKeyName="//iam.googleapis.com/projects/P/serviceAccounts/SA/keys/KEY_ID"; per-key counts: Metrics Explorer > Service account key authentication events

reads.ui: IAM & Admin > Audit Logs > select service > Permission types: Data Read > Save; then Logs Explorer filter serviceAccountKeyName
reads.api: Add auditConfigs {logType: DATA_READ} to the project/folder/org IAM policy (setIamPolicy)

token_format.notes: JSON file with "type": "service_account", private_key_id (key ID) and client_email.

log_sources.name: Cloud Audit Logs - Admin Activity
log_sources.notes: Always on; key create/delete/disable. _Required bucket keeps 400 days.

log_sources.name: Cloud Audit Logs - Data Access
log_sources.notes: Off by default except BigQuery; needed to see reads. _Default bucket 30 days.

log_sources.name: Cloud Monitoring 'Service account key authentication events'

credential_id_fields.log: Cloud Audit Logs of called service
credential_id_fields.notes: Full key resource name; missing for App Engine and Compute Engine.

anomaly_cues: Key used from a new callerIp
Key created then used from outside your network

containment.steps: Disable the SA (cuts all tokens), then delete the key; rotate dependents.
containment.notes: Key deletion alone leaves minted tokens valid (up to 1h, or 12h if extended).

calls.log_notes: Not covered by Cloud Audit Logs docs

calls.reveals: All resources visible to the SA
calls.log_notes: ADMIN_READ Data Access log; off by default
Listing buckets is ADMIN_READ Data Access; off by default
DATA_READ Data Access; off by default (BigQuery is on by default)

credentials.name: Short-lived service account credentials (service account impersonation)

authentication.summary: A principal with the Service Account Token Creator role calls the IAM Credentials API (generateAccessToken, generateIdToken, signJwt) to mint a short-lived token for a service account.

federation.details: The caller authenticates first (user, SA or federated identity), so the caller's own login controls apply at minting time. The minted SA token is then used without user CAA checks.

ip_restriction.boundary: Only via VPC Service Controls perimeters on supported services.

renewal.summary: Caller mints a new token while it still holds the Token Creator permission.

administration.summary: Control who holds roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on each SA. Issued tokens cannot be revoked one by one; disable or delete the SA.

offboard.details: The token is issued for a service account, not a user.

expiry.ui: Organization policies > constraints/iam.allowServiceAccountCredentialLifetimeExtension > Manage policy (list SAs allowed up to 12h)

usage.ui: Enable Data Access (Admin Read) for IAM Service Account Credentials API under IAM & Admin > Audit Logs; then Logs Explorer: protoPayload.serviceName="iamcredentials.googleapis.com" protoPayload.methodName="GenerateAccessToken"

reads.ui: Enable Data Read for Cloud Storage (IAM & Admin > Audit Logs); Logs Explorer: protoPayload.serviceName="storage.googleapis.com" and protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=SA_EMAIL

kill.ui: IAM & Admin > Service accounts > (SA) > Service account status > Disable service account; remove Token Creator grants on the SA
kill.cli: gcloud iam service-accounts disable SA_EMAIL; gcloud iam service-accounts remove-iam-policy-binding SA_EMAIL --member=PRINCIPAL --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator

token_format.notes: OAuth 2.0 access token or OIDC ID token; not documented as prefixed.

log_sources.name: IAM Data Access audit logs (iamcredentials.googleapis.com)
log_sources.notes: Must be enabled; records each token mint.

credential_id_fields.notes: SA the token was minted for

anomaly_cues: New principal minting tokens for a privileged SA

containment.steps: Remove Token Creator bindings; disable the SA to kill live tokens.
containment.notes: Disabling the SA is the documented kill for short-lived credentials.

calls.reveals: Whether caller can impersonate the SA
calls.log_notes: Data Access log; must be enabled

calls.reveals: Object names and metadata in a bucket
calls.log_notes: Listing objects is a DATA_READ Data Access audit log entry; Data Access logs are off by default and must be enabled.

detections.detects: A service account was disabled or deleted.

authentication.summary: An external workload (AWS, Azure, GitHub, other OIDC/SAML IdP) sends its IdP token to the Security Token Service and gets a federated token, used directly on resources or to impersonate a service account.

federation.details: Trust is based on the external IdP token plus provider attribute conditions; no Google user SSO is involved.

ip_restriction.boundary: VPC Service Controls perimeters only; no IP setting on the pool itself was found.

lifetime.summary: Federated bearer tokens valid up to 1 hour

renewal.expiry_basis: New exchange with a fresh external IdP token

administration.summary: Org policy allow-lists IdP issuers and AWS accounts; pools/providers can be disabled or deleted; attribute conditions restrict which external identities can exchange.
administration.conditions: Org policies need an organization resource.

offboard.details: Credentials come from external workloads' federated identities, not Google user accounts.

inventory.details: Pools and providers are listable org-wide in Cloud Asset Inventory; issued federated tokens are not.

inventory.ui: IAM & Admin > Workload Identity Federation (Workload Identity Pools page); org-wide: Asset Inventory search for iam.googleapis.com/WorkloadIdentityPool and WorkloadIdentityPoolProvider
inventory.cli: gcloud iam workload-identity-pools list --location=global; gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers list --workload-identity-pool=POOL --location=global

disable.ui: Organization policies > constraints/iam.workloadIdentityPoolProviders > Manage policy (Deny all or list allowed issuer URIs)

expiry.api: POST https://sts.googleapis.com/v1/token returns expires_in (seconds until the federated token expires)

usage.ui: Enable Data Access for Security Token Service API (IAM & Admin > Audit Logs); Logs Explorer: protoPayload.serviceName="sts.googleapis.com" protoPayload.methodName="google.identity.sts.v1.SecurityTokenService.ExchangeToken", read principalSubject

reads.ui: Enable Data Read for Cloud Storage (IAM & Admin > Audit Logs); Logs Explorer: protoPayload.serviceName="storage.googleapis.com", filter on the federated principal or impersonated SA

kill.ui: Workload Identity Pools > (pool) > Status toggle > Disable (provider: same on provider details); also disable any impersonated SA
kill.cli: gcloud iam workload-identity-pools update POOL --location=global --disabled; gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers update-oidc PROVIDER --workload-identity-pool=POOL --location=global --disabled

token_format.notes: Federated access token from STS; not documented as prefixed.

log_sources.name: Data Access logs for STS API and IAM API (Admin Read)
log_sources.notes: Must be enabled to log exchanges.

credential_id_fields.notes: External subject (AWS ARN, Azure object ID, OIDC sub)

Provider without attribute condition on a multi-tenant IdP

containment.steps: Disable the provider or pool; tighten attribute condition; disable impersonated SA to kill live tokens.
containment.notes: Disabling the pool blocks existing tokens (until re-enabled); disabling a provider only stops new exchanges and existing tokens keep working. Tokens from impersonated service accounts need separate action.

credentials.name: API keys (standard keys and authorization keys bound to a service account)

authentication.summary: A bearer string (AIza...) sent with requests. Standard keys only identify a project for billing/quota; authorization keys act as the bound service account, similar to a long-lived access token.

federation.details: Standard keys identify no principal; authorization keys act as a service account. Neither is tied to user SSO.

ip_restriction.boundary: Per-key application restrictions (external IPs, referrers, Android/iOS apps) and API restrictions. Keys created by REST API are unrestricted unless set. Internal IPs are not supported.

lifetime.summary: No expiry setting found on fetched pages

renewal.summary: Console 'Rotate key' creates a new key with the same restrictions; then delete the old one.

administration.summary: Binding keys to service accounts is blocked by a default org policy (Gemini API allowed by default). Standard key creation needs serviceusage.apiKeys.create.
administration.conditions: Changing the constraint needs an organization resource.

offboard.details: Standard keys don't identify a principal; authorization keys act as a service account.

inventory.details: Cloud Asset Inventory supports apikeys.googleapis.com/Key; per project also gcloud services api-keys list.

usage.ui: Logs Explorer: protoPayload.serviceName="apikeys.googleapis.com" (CreateKey/DeleteKey/UpdateKey are Admin Activity; GetKeyString needs Data Access Admin Read enabled)

log_sources.name: Cloud Audit Logs (apikeys.googleapis.com)
log_sources.notes: CreateKey/DeleteKey/UpdateKey are Admin Activity; GetKeyString is Data Access.

credential_id_fields.notes: Docs say authorization keys obscure end-user identity; data-plane key field not documented.

lifecycle_events.notes: Someone read the key string; Data Access

anomaly_cues: Authorization key created after constraint change

containment.steps: Delete the key (or add restrictions); for authorization keys also disable the bound SA.
containment.notes: Propagation time for deletion not documented.

unknown: Which log field shows the API key on API calls
No documented whoami for API keys; reachable APIs depend on key restrictions

authentication.summary: Access ID + secret used to sign Cloud Storage XML API requests (S3-compatible). Usually tied to a service account; user-account HMAC keys also exist.

federation.details: Signed requests carry no IdP session. No doc ties HMAC use to SSO or CAA.

ip_restriction.boundary: No per-key IP list found. VPC Service Controls can restrict Cloud Storage access by network.

lifetime.summary: No expiry documented on fetched pages; valid until deactivated or deleted

renewal.summary: Rotate by creating a new key, updating clients, then deleting the old key.

administration.summary: disableServiceAccountKeyCreation also blocks SA HMAC key creation; storage.restrictAuthTypes rejects HMAC-signed requests org-wide.
administration.conditions: Org policies need an organization resource.

offboard.details: Deleting the account deletes its HMAC keys, and docs warn user-account keys break when the user is disabled after leaving.

inventory.details: HMAC keys are listed per project (gcloud storage hmac list / ListHmacKeys); HMAC keys are not in the Cloud Asset Inventory asset type list.

offboard.ui: Google Admin console > Directory > Users > (user) > More options > Delete user (deleting the account deletes its HMAC keys)

token_format.notes: Access ID 61 chars for SA, 24 chars for user; example starts GOOG. Secret is 40-char base64.
